title: Candidate evidence + decision guide and compact 30/90 onboard
body:
Purpose
This is a compact, operational guide for small hiring sprints (2–4 ICs at once) that ties interview evidence directly to decision heuristics and a pragmatic 30/90 onboarding checklist. The goal: reduce stalled offers and inconsistent hiring signals during rapid growth while preserving fair, evidence-based decisions.

Audience
People Ops (recruiting + hiring ops), hiring managers, interview panel leads, and solutions engineering for role-specific probes.

High-level sprint goals (example)
- Fill 3 backend engineer ICs in 6 weeks (sourcing -> offer -> start).
- Time-to-offer target: 18 days from first screen.
- Candidate conversion target: 25% of onsite -> offers accepted.

Sourcing notes (quick ops)
- Use targeted outreach: previous Redwood contributors, referrals, top 5 feeder schools.
- Prioritize candidates with production-serving experience (latency/throughput tradeoffs).
- Tag pipelines for hire level (IC2/IC3/Senior) so we can reuse rubric thresholds.
- Slack shorthand for recruiter threads: [team]-hire-[req#] (e.g., serving-hire-231).

Interview flow (compact 3-hop model)
1) Recruiter screen (30m): culture fit, logistics, basic system design sense. Score pass/fail + 1–3 quick evidence bullets.
2) Technical screen (45m): whiteboard-ish problem + follow-ups. Use consistent prompt from library. Record 3 core observations: approach, trade-offs, communication.
3) Onsite / loop (4 interviews, 40m each):
   - System design (team-specific)
   - Implementation + debugging (pairing)
   - Behavioral + collaboration
   - Product/mission fit (PM or engineering lead)
Panel should include at least one cross-functional stakeholder when hiring for infra or platform roles.

Evidence matrix (what to capture in notes)
- Correctness: Demonstrated correct approach or recovered from mistakes (concrete examples).
- Depth: Knowledge about production constraints (caching, batching, observability).
- Tradeoffs: Explicit tradeoff reasoning, e.g., latency vs cost, eventual consistency choices.
- Ownership/impact: Past examples of shipping features, incident ownership.
- Communication: Can explain design to non-experts, concise summaries.
- Learning agility: Evidence of learning new stacks or debugging unfamiliar systems.

Scoring rubric (numeric guide, keep simple)
- 4 = Strong hire (exceeds expectations for level; immediate impact)
- 3 = Good hire (meets expectations; few gaps, quick ramp)
- 2 = Borderline (some concerning gaps; needs significant mentorship)
- 1 = Not hire (does not meet bar)
Scoring rules: average of interview scores is advisory. Hiring manager override allowed but requires written justification (1–3 bullets) in the candidate record.

Decision heuristics (concrete rules to reduce bias)
- Must-haves (all hires): ownership story + at least one production constraint discussion. If missing both, fail.
- Level-specific thresholds: Senior (>=3.25 average + at least one 4), IC3 (>=3.0), IC2 (>=2.5).
- Red flag override: documented behavioral red flags (team conflict, ethical issues) require a People Ops escalation and cannot be waived by a single manager.
- Tie-breaker: prefer candidates who show demonstrable impact on metrics (latency/cost/regressions) in past roles.

Offer cadence and docs
- Target: present offer within 48 hours after panel debrief. Comp packet must include: base, equity range, comp band rationale, sign-on bonus (if any), and ramp expectations.
- Use standard template in Confluence and link payband justification to job leveling doc.

Compact 30/90 onboarding checklist (for ICs)
First week (day 0–7):
- Day 0: HR welcome email, equipment shipping confirmation, Slack + SSO invites, access to core repos.
- Day 1: Manager 1:1 (30m) — expectations + 30/90 goals; buddy assigned; calendar of 1:1s scheduled.
- Week tasks: small first task (bugfix or docs edit) with pair review; access to dev envs and test clusters; security/readme walkthrough.
- Checkpoint: end-of-week quick sync (30m) with manager + buddy.

First 30 days:
- Complete cognitive onboarding checklist: infra diagrams, common runbooks, latency/cost playbook read.
- Deliverable: ship a nontrivial change (bugfix, perf tweak, or doc) with PR reviewed by 2 reviewers.
- Milestone: ramp call with manager to confirm trajectory and any blockers.

First 90 days:
- Ownership: assigned a small service or feature area to own operationally.
- Metrics: baseline metric to improve (p95 latency or e2e cost) documented and an experiment proposal submitted.
- Career conversation: manager writes an initial success evidence note to Talent within 90 days.

Manager checklist (fast ops)
- Week 1: setup clear first task + review criteria; introduce to cross-functional partners; ensure tooling access.
- Weeks 2–4: weekly feedback notes (quick score out of 5) to track progress; escalate missing progress at week 4.
- 30/60/90: written checkpoint stored in candidate record (Confluence template).

Risk mitigation and fallback plans
- If a hire is underperforming at 30/60, run a structured performance plan with clear objectives and a 4-week follow-up. People Ops to support with coaching resources.
- Pool hires: when multiple qualified candidates available, tag as “pool:fast-start” to fill upcoming near-term seat openings without repeating full loop.

Notes to self / open questions
- Should we always include a short take-home exercise for senior infra roles? Pros: deeper signal. Cons: lengthens funnel and lowers conversion. Need pilot (A/B) in Q2.
- How to better document bias independence in decision notes? Maybe add a quick checkbox for "evidence-backed hiring" vs "reputation-based".
- Action: ask Legal if the offer template needs an updated international clause for EMEA hires (ticket HR-4683).

Quick links
- Recruiting tracker: https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/secure/RapidBoard.jspa?rapidView=14
- Onboarding template (Confluence): confluence:HR/compact-onboard-templates
- Interview prompt library: drive:shared_drives/company/misc/interview-prompts-2025

Appendix: Example panel note (copyable)
- Q: Brief summary of role fit (2–3 lines).
- Evidence bullets: 3–5 short bullets mapping to Evidence matrix items above.
- Score: 1–4 and one sentence justification.
- Recommendation: hire / no-hire / hire-with-conditions (list conditions).

End.

(Quick draft — this is intentionally concise and operational. Will expand if we pilot and need specific level templates for Platform vs Product teams.)
